name: Maggie - Waterfalls: Nelly to Arcadia
description:
Leader: Cherry

Description :
Beginning at the ferry terminal in Nelly Bay, we’ll make our way over the ridge to Arcadia. We'll check out Endeavour Falls, a seasonal waterfall that will be flowing nicely following recent rainfall. We'll check out Sphinx lookout and then we’ll go down to Geoffrey Bay make our way back

WHAT TO EXPECT:

Easy to moderate grade hike between Nelly and Arcadia. it depends on how much uphill's you are used to and the heat
Approximate distance/duration: 10kms, 4 hours.
While the weather is currently predicted to cloudy with a bit of rain - not much compared to last week, come prepared for either a hot walk or a wet one.
There are exposed sections, so expect it to be hot.
The pace will be moderate and continuous, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops at the points of interest along the way.
I think we might end up back at Nelly by about 10-11 am for a bit at SOS

Additional information about Magnetic Island

Magnetic Island Waterfalls (wanderstories.space)
What to see on Magnetic Island (wanderstories.space)

WHAT TO BRING:
Water (2-3 Litres recommended)
A hat and sunscreen
Insect repellent
Trail snacks and morning tea
Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces
Dry clothes and perhaps a pair of thongs for after the walk
First aid kit/snake bite kit if you have one
Ginger/motion sickness tablets for the ferry if you get seasick
Petty cash is never a bad idea for the island.
RSVP:
**RSVP here - https://forms.gle/xWRQC82dG9sS6DrTA**

If you have never walked with the TBWC before, please reach out to the walk leader to ascertain the suitability of this walk for you before you RSVP - Cherry Judge - info@veteducation.com.au

Visitors are welcome - it is $5 to cover our club insurance.
You can do 3 walks and qualify to become a TBWC member!

name: Mount Paulma, Magnetic Island
description:
Mount Paluma (Magnetic Island) summit walk

Leader: Luen Warneke
Start time: Saturday, 8:30 am
Location: Magnetic Island National Park
Distance: ~6 km return
Duration: Allow 4 hours
Grade: 4 – moderate to difficult
Terrain: Steep, rocky, overgrown sections; off-track navigation
Conditions: Rain forecast – track likely wet and slippery
RSVP by emailing luenwarneke@gmail.com for meetup details.

Mount Paluma (322 m) is one of only two officially named mountains on Magnetic Island, yet it remains largely unknown and rarely visited. This walk follows remnants of an old ridgeline route that has long since been reclaimed by vegetation, making it an engaging mix of faint pad, rock steps, stacked stone retaining walls, and off-track navigation.

The ascent is steady and sometimes steep, passing grass trees and open woodland before climbing to a saddle below the summit. Although the historic track is no longer maintained, evidence of earlier construction is still visible, adding a strong sense of place and history to the walk.

From the summit area, walkers are rewarded with expansive views across Nelly Bay, Townsville, Alma Bay, Horseshoe Bay, and out across the Coral Sea. A rock cairn marks the high point, with nearby boulders offering excellent vantage points for a short break if conditions allow.

With rain forecast, expect slippery rock, muddy sections, and slower progress. Careful foot placement will be essential, and walking poles are recommended. The walk will proceed at a steady, conservative pace suitable for the conditions.

Requirements:
2 L water per person
Snacks
Long pants and long-sleeve shirt
Rain jacket optional
Hat and sunscreen
Insect repellent
Good grip footwear
Navigation tools
First aid kit and PLB

More information: https://wanderstories.space/mt-paluma-magnetic-island/


This is a Grade 4 walk involving off-track travel and uneven terrain. Participants should be comfortable with rough ground, variable conditions, and changing weather. Leave No Trace principles apply – please carry out all rubbish.
